questions.text:
Which of the following fields is/are modified in the IP header of a packet going out
of a network address translation (NAT) device from an internal network to an
external network?
questions.solution:
For an outgoing packet, NAT replaces the private source IP (and port) with its public IP.

Because a header field changed, the header checksum must be recomputed.

Destination IP is unchanged (it is the outside server), and total length is unchanged (payload size is the same).

Answer: Source IP, Header Checksum

questions.text: Let [latex]A [/latex] and [latex]B [/latex] be non-empty finite sets such that there exist one-to-one and onto functions (i) from [latex]A [/latex] to [latex]B [/latex] and (ii) from [latex]A \times A [/latex] to [latex]A \cup B [/latex]. The number of possible values of [latex]|A| [/latex] is ___
questions.solution:
Bijection [latex]A\to B[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]|A|=|B|=n[/latex].
Bijection [latex]A\times A\to A\cup B[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]n^2=|A\cup B|[/latex].

But [latex]n\le|A\cup B|\le 2n[/latex], so [latex]n\le n^2\le 2n[/latex] [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] [latex]n\le2[/latex].

- [latex]n=1[/latex]: [latex]A=B[/latex], [latex]|A\cup B|=1=1^2[/latex] True
- [latex]n=2[/latex]: take A and B disjoint, [latex]|A\cup B|=4=2^2[/latex] True

So [latex]|A|\in\{1,2\}[/latex].

Answer: 2

questions.text:
Consider the operator precedence and associativity rules for the integer arithmetic operators given in the table below.
[latex]\begin{array}{|c|l|l|} \hline Operator & Precedence & Associativity \\ \hline+ & Highest & Left \\ \hline- & High & Right \\ \hline* & Medium & Right \\ \hline / & Low & Right \\ \hline \end{array} [/latex]
The value of the expression [latex]3+1+5 * 2 / 7+2-4-7-6 / 2 [/latex] as per the above rules is _____
questions.solution:
Precedence: + (highest) [latex]\gt[/latex] [latex]-[/latex] [latex]\gt[/latex] * [latex]\gt[/latex] / (lowest). The lowest-precedence operator is applied last, so / splits the expression:
[latex](3+1+5*2)\;/\;(7+2-4-7-6)\;/\;2[/latex]

First part: + binds before *, so [latex](3+1+5)*2=9*2=18[/latex].
Second part: + first: [latex]7+2=9[/latex]. Then [latex]-[/latex] is right associative: [latex]9-(4-(7-6))=9-(4-1)=6[/latex].

/ is right associative: [latex]18/(6/2)=18/3=6[/latex].

Answer: 6

questions.text:
The number of spanning trees in a complete graph of 4 vertices labelled A, B, C,
and D is _________
questions.solution:
Number of spanning trees of a complete graph [latex]K_n[/latex] (Cayley's formula) [latex]=n^{n-2}[/latex].

[latex]4^{4-2}=16[/latex]

Answer: 16

questions.text:
Consider the following two relations, [latex]R(A, B) [/latex] and [latex]S(A, C) [/latex] :
[latex]\boldsymbol{R} \begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline \boldsymbol{A} & \boldsymbol{B} \\ \hline 10 & 20 \\ \hline 20 & 30 \\ \hline 30 & 40 \\ \hline 30 & 50 \\ \hline 50 & 95 \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]


[latex]\boldsymbol{S} \begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline \boldsymbol{A} & \boldsymbol{C} \\ \hline 10 & 90 \\ \hline 30 & 45 \\ \hline 40 & 80 \\ \hline \end{array} [/latex]
The total number of tuples obtained by evaluating the following expression [latex] \sigma_{B \lt C}\left(R \bowtie_{R . A=S . A} S\right) [/latex] is ____
questions.solution:
Join on [latex]R.A=S.A[/latex]:
- A = 10: (10, 20, 90) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]20 \lt 90[/latex] True
- A = 30: (30, 40, 45) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]40 \lt 45[/latex] True
- A = 30: (30, 50, 45) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]50 \lt 45[/latex] False
(A = 20, 50 in R and A = 40 in S have no match.)

Answer: 2
